advances: The proposed ambient full-row price is false even for complete full-dimensional convex lattice supports having exactly two atoms in every ambient parity class. A single global affine field gives ambient activity, bounded full reflected surplus, and an unbounded full-row score price. This refutes the stated restricted price, while leaving the locked depth conjecture open. The same examples admit zero-score auxiliary rows with ambient reflected energy greater than one, so this is specifically an obstruction to requiring all full rows.
author: research-agent
external_sources: None. Every geometric census, global affine realization, full-row quantity, and asymptotic estimate is proved above. The two declared accepted predecessors supply only the unchanged notation and the price being tested.
proof:
The parameters satisfy \(a=Ku\), \(K=u^{-5}\), and \(2^{n-2}=K/4\). The restriction \(h\ge2\) ensures \(4h\le n-2\), so \(\mathcal R\) in (2) is defined and has exactly \(a\) elements. The three disjoint layers have cardinalities \(|M|=K\), \(|T|=K-a\), and \(|B|=a\).

We first prove the entire lattice census. The height \(z\) lies in \([-1,1]\) throughout \(Q\). Its top slice is exactly \(\operatorname{conv}(T)\), and its bottom slice is exactly \(\operatorname{conv}(B)\), since these are the extreme heights.

Project the top slice to its \((x,y)\) coordinates. It lies inside \([0,1]^{n-2}\times[0,3]\), so every lattice point in it has Boolean \(x\) and \(y\in\lbrace0,1,2,3\rbrace\). Every such point is in \(T\), except for the removed points \((x,3)\) with \(x\in\mathcal R\). Each removed point is an extreme vertex of the larger box \([0,1]^{n-2}\times[0,3]\). It cannot lie in the convex hull of the other points of that box, and hence cannot lie in \(\operatorname{conv}(T)\). This proves the exact top census. The bottom slice is the box \(-\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal R)\times\lbrace-1\rbrace\), whose lattice points are exactly those listed in \(B\).

For the zero slice, write \(P_M=[0,1]^{n-2}\times[0,3]\), and let \(P_T,P_B\) denote the horizontal projections of the other two layer hulls. A convex combination having height zero uses equal total coefficients on the top and bottom slices. Therefore the horizontal zero slice is
\(\operatorname{conv}(P_M,\tfrac12(P_T+P_B))\).
In its first \(4h\) coordinates, \(\tfrac12(P_T+P_B)\) lies in \([-1/2,1/2]\); in its remaining \(h-2\) horizontal \(x\) coordinates it lies in \([0,1/2]\); and its \(y\) coordinate lies in \([-1/2,1]\). The entire zero slice is consequently contained in
$$
[-1/2,1]^{4h}\times[0,1]^{h-2}\times[-1/2,3].
\tag{8}
$$
The lattice points of the box (8) are exactly the horizontal points of \(M\), all of which are present in \(Q\). This proves the exact zero census. The heights \(-1,0,1\) exhaust all integer heights, so \(Q\cap\mathbb Z^n=A\). The top slice contains \([0,1]^{n-2}\times[0,2]\), of dimension \(n-1\), and the middle layer supplies a different height. Thus \(Q\) is full-dimensional. It is the convex hull of finitely many integer points, proving the remaining polytope assertions.

We next enumerate every parity class and hence every nontrivial integral midpoint pair. The middle layer has even \(z\) parity. For each Boolean \(x\), its even-\(y\) class consists of \((x,0,0),(x,2,0)\), and its odd-\(y\) class consists of \((x,1,0),(x,3,0)\). There are \(2^{n-1}=K/2\) such classes, each of size two. The outer layers have odd \(z\) parity. If \(x\notin\mathcal R\), their two classes at that Boolean \(x\) are the two top pairs with \(y\) values \(0,2\) and \(1,3\). If \(x\in\mathcal R\), the even-\(y\) class is the top pair with \(y\) values \(0,2\), whereas the odd-\(y\) class is
\(\lbrace(x,1,1),(-x,-1,-1)\rbrace\).
Negation preserves coordinate parity, so this list includes every bottom atom and produces exactly two atoms in each of the other \(K/2\) classes.

Two distinct lattice atoms have an integral midpoint if and only if they have the same parity. Since all parity classes have exactly two atoms, the preceding list is exhaustive. Its middle pairs have centers \((x,1,0)\) and \((x,2,0)\), one pair at each of \(K/2\) distinct middle centers. The internal top pairs have centers \((x,1,1)\) for all Boolean \(x\), and additionally \((x,2,1)\) for \(x\notin\mathcal R\). These are \(K/2-a\) distinct top centers, one pair at each. Finally, all \(a\) cross-layer pairs have common midpoint \(0=(0,0,0)\). This origin is different from every middle center just listed.

Consequently the full row cardinalities are \(2a+1\) at the origin, three at the \(K/2-a\) top centers and \(K/2\) middle centers, and one at every other atom. The origin remains an endpoint of its middle pair with \((0,2,0)\), whose midpoint is \((0,1,0)\). This pair has already been counted among the middle pairs; being a center of cross-layer pairs does not remove that endpoint incidence. Every atom is an endpoint of exactly one nontrivial pair, so in the incidence notation of 445a9e668ee1a705 the maximum \(D\) equals one and the maximum row cardinality is \(r=2a+1\), which diverges.

The weights (4) are one global affine exponential law. Each top atom has weight one, each middle atom weight \(u\), and each bottom atom weight \(u^2\). Their counts give
\(Z=(K-a)+Ku+au^2=K(1+u^3)\), with no change of normalization. Their raw cubic sum is
$$
J_3:=\sum_{v\in A}w_v^3
=(K-a)+Ku^3+au^6
=K(1-u+u^3+u^7).
\tag{9}
$$
The first formula (5) follows from \(A_0=K^2J_3/Z^3\). For \(0<u\le1/4\), the denominator minus its numerator is
\(u+2u^3+3u^6-u^7+u^9>0\), since \(3u^6-u^7>0\). This proves strict activity for every stated \(h\).

For every pair with midpoint \(j\), global affinity gives \(w_xw_{2j-x}=w_j^2\). Thus every geometric-mean summand in its full row is exactly \(p_j\), \(H_p(j)=|R_j|p_j\), and \(\kappa_j\) is uniform on the entire row. This uses precisely the full-row meanings of both declared accepted predecessors. Starting from the singleton-row cubic sum (9), a three-point row adds \(8w_j^3\) to \(Z^3b(p)\), and the origin row adds \(4a(a+1)u^3\). Hence
$$
\begin{aligned}
Z^3b(p)
&=J_3+8(K/2-a)+8(K/2)u^3+4a(a+1)u^3\\
&=K\bigl(9-9u+5u^3+4u^4+u^7\bigr).
\end{aligned}
\tag{10}
$$
For the last equality, \(a(a+1)u^3/K=1+u^4\), by \(a=Ku\) and \(K=u^{-5}\). Dividing (10) by the unchanged \(Z^3\) and multiplying by the ambient \(K^2=4^n\) proves the second formula (5).

All nontrivial rows other than the origin row lie in a fixed \(z\) layer and therefore have identically zero scores. At the origin, the \(a\) upper endpoints have score \(t=\log(1/u)\), the \(a\) lower endpoints have score \(-t\), and the central atom has score zero. Uniformity of \(\kappa_0\) gives
$$
V_0=\frac{2a}{2a+1}t^2,\qquad
\nu(p)=\frac{(2a+1)^2(u/Z)^3}{b(p)}V_0
=\frac{2a(2a+1)u^3}{Z^3b(p)}t^2.
\tag{11}
$$
Now \(2a(2a+1)u^3/K=4+2u^4\). Combining (10) and (11) proves the last formula (5), including its original probabilities and full auxiliary center law.

For completeness, when \(0<u\le1/4\), \((1+u^3)^3<2\) and the numerator of \(A_{\mathrm{full}}\) is at least \(27/4\). Thus \(A_{\mathrm{full}}>27/8>1\). Its numerator is less than ten and its denominator at least one, so \(A_{\mathrm{full}}<10\). Letting \(h\to\infty\) in the exact expressions proves all the limits in (6). This refutes the proposed absolute price, rather than merely giving a large fixed constant.

Finally, select only the central atom in the origin row and retain every other full row. This deletes precisely the last increment in (10), leaving
$$
Z^3\widehat b
=J_3+8(K/2-a)+8(K/2)u^3
=K(5-9u+5u^3+u^7).
\tag{12}
$$
The original origin mass and its endpoint role in the middle row remain untouched. All selected row scores are zero, so \(\widehat\nu=0\). The numerator in (7) is at least \(11/4\), while its denominator is less than two; hence its energy is greater than one for every \(h\ge2\). Equation (12) proves (7) and its limit.

To verify the product calibration directly, let \(P=\bigotimes_{i=1}^L p_i\) be any finite product of the original laws (4), with \(N=\sum_i n_i\). At a supported target \(J=(j_i)_i\), take the product of the selected symmetric rows. Its selected reflected mass is \(\widehat H_P(J)=\prod_i\widehat H_{p_i}(j_i)\). Each factor row lies in one fixed \(z\) layer or is a singleton, so every point in this product row has original mass \(P_J\). Every ambient closed halfspace containing \(J\) contains at least one endpoint of each noncentral reflection pair and the central atom. Its original mass is therefore at least \(\widehat H_P(J)/2\). Squaring this inequality and summing against the original product law gives \(M_2(P)\ge\tfrac14\prod_i\widehat b_i\ge\tfrac14 4^{-N}\), using (7). Jensen under the same original law gives \(M_3(P)\ge M_2(P)^{3/2}\ge\tfrac18 8^{-N}\). Only selected reflected masses factorize here; no factorization of actual depths or moments is assumed.
statement:
Use exactly the full-row conventions of accepted facts 445a9e668ee1a705 and 0a0cf4ab8ae7921f. For a positive law \(p_x=w_x/Z\) on a finite support \(A\subseteq\mathbb Z^n\), extended by zero off \(A\), these are
$$
\begin{aligned}
R_j&=\lbrace x\in A:2j-x\in A\rbrace,&
H_p(j)&=\sum_{x\in R_j}\sqrt{p_xp_{2j-x}},&
b(p)&=\sum_{j\in A}p_jH_p(j)^2,\\
\kappa_j(x)&=\frac{\sqrt{p_xp_{2j-x}}}{H_p(j)},&
Y_j(x)&=\frac12\log\frac{p_x}{p_{2j-x}},&
V_j&=\mathbb E_{\kappa_j}Y_j^2,\\
q_j&=\frac{p_jH_p(j)^2}{b(p)},&
\nu(p)&=\sum_{j\in A}q_jV_j.
\end{aligned}
\tag{1}
$$
Thus the \(\nu(p)\) here is the scalar score price of 0a0cf4ab8ae7921f and the one-factor left side of (7) in 445a9e668ee1a705. All row sums are oriented, retaining the central atom once and both orientations of each nonzero pair. Below \(K=2^n\) is the ambient parity capacity, not an occupied-count replacement.

For every integer \(h\ge2\), put
$$
\begin{gathered}
n=5h,\qquad K=2^n,\qquad a=2^{4h},\qquad u=2^{-h},\\
\mathcal R=\lbrace0,1\rbrace^{4h}\times\lbrace0\rbrace^{h-2}
\subseteq\lbrace0,1\rbrace^{n-2}.
\end{gathered}
\tag{2}
$$
The power \(\lbrace0\rbrace^0\) has its usual singleton meaning when \(h=2\). In coordinates \((x,y,z)\in\mathbb R^{n-2}\times\mathbb R\times\mathbb R\), define
$$
\begin{aligned}
M&=\lbrace(x,y,0):x\in\lbrace0,1\rbrace^{n-2},\ y\in\lbrace0,1,2,3\rbrace\rbrace,\\
T&=\lbrace(x,y,1):x\in\lbrace0,1\rbrace^{n-2},\ y\in\lbrace0,1,2,3\rbrace,\ (x,y)\notin\mathcal R\times\lbrace3\rbrace\rbrace,\\
B&=\lbrace(-x,-1,-1):x\in\mathcal R\rbrace,\qquad
A=M\cup T\cup B,\qquad Q=\operatorname{conv}(A).
\end{aligned}
\tag{3}
$$
Then \(Q\) is a compact full-dimensional rational lattice polytope, \(A=Q\cap\mathbb Z^n\), and every one of the \(K\) ambient parity classes contains exactly two atoms of \(A\).

Give this support the single global affine raw law
$$
w_{(x,y,z)}=u^{1-z}
=\exp\bigl(\log u-(\log u)z\bigr),\qquad
Z=\sum_{v\in A}w_v=K(1+u^3),\qquad p_v=w_v/Z.
\tag{4}
$$
Thus the constant and linear coefficients in the global affine convention of 0a0cf4ab8ae7921f are \(c=\log u\) and \(\ell=(0,\ldots,0,-\log u)\); its normalizer \(W\) is exactly the original \(Z\) in (4). No probability law is changed or conditioned.

Writing \(A_0=4^n\sum_{v\in A}p_v^3\) and \(A_{\mathrm{full}}=4^n b(p)\), the following formulas are exact:
$$
\begin{aligned}
A_0&=\frac{1-u+u^3+u^7}{(1+u^3)^3}<1,\\
A_{\mathrm{full}}&=\frac{9-9u+5u^3+4u^4+u^7}{(1+u^3)^3},\\
\nu(p)&=\frac{4+2u^4}{9-9u+5u^3+4u^4+u^7}
\left(\log\frac1u\right)^2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{5}
$$
In particular \(1<A_{\mathrm{full}}<10\), \(A_0\to1\) from below, \(A_{\mathrm{full}}\to9\), and
$$
\frac{\nu(p)}{\log A_{\mathrm{full}}}
\sim\frac{4}{9\log9}\left(h\log2\right)^2
\longrightarrow+\infty.
\tag{6}
$$
There is consequently no finite absolute \(C\ge0\) such that \(\nu(p)\le C\log(4^n b(p))\) for all complete convex globally affine laws of parity occupancy at most two satisfying \(A_0<1\).

For calibration only, retain every full row except at the origin, where retain only its central atom. Let \(\widehat b\) and \(\widehat\nu\) be defined from these selected symmetric rows by the same formulas (1), under the same original law (4). Then
$$
4^n\widehat b=\frac{5-9u+5u^3+u^7}{(1+u^3)^3}>1,
\qquad \widehat\nu=0,
\qquad 4^n\widehat b\longrightarrow5.
\tag{7}
$$
Moreover, for any finite independent product \(P\) of members of this family, of total ambient dimension \(N\), the original ambient-halfspace moments in 445a9e668ee1a705 satisfy \(M_2(P)\ge\tfrac14 4^{-N}\) and \(M_3(P)\ge\tfrac18 8^{-N}\). Thus (5)-(6) are not a counterexample to an actual depth moment estimate or to a method allowed to select rows.
